business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 2007, the Company manufactures aluminium and copper-based electrical winding wires, conductors and cables, including LT cables (including LT Aerial Bunched cables up to 1.1 kV), HT cables and Medium Voltage Covered Conductor (MVCC) cables, as well as winding aluminium/copper wires and strips and aluminium conductors. It supplies primarily to state-owned DISCOMs (via tender-based procurement) and private-sector EPC/infrastructure entities (via purchase orders), and also undertakes trading of aluminium wires and rods and job-work processing of winding wires and strips.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cables:** Low Tension (LT) cables, Low Tension Aerial Bunched (LT AB) cables (up to 1.1 kV), High Tension (HT) cables, Medium Voltage Covered Conductor (MVCC) Cables
- **Wires and Conductors:** Winding aluminium wires and strips, Winding copper wires and strips, Aluminium conductors
- **Trading and Job Work:** Trading of aluminium wires and rods, Job work services - processing of winding wires and strips

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Trading of aluminium wires and rods (key raw materials for own production) alongside manufacturing; job work services provided for processing of customers' winding wires & strips. Raw materials (aluminium and copper rods, kraft paper, insulating varnish, PVC filler, XLPE and PVC compound) are procured from multiple domestic suppliers at prevailing market prices; all manufacturing facilities and machinery are fully owned by the Company. Manufacturing process spans raw material procurement, wire drawing/conductor drawing, stranding, annealing, in-process quality inspection, insulation/enamelling or extrusion, curing, final testing, and packing and dispatch.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shift away from Government/DISCOM customers (90.55% of revenue in FY24 down to 35.78% in FY26) toward private sector entities (9.45% up to 64.22%)
- Rising share of trading revenue from aluminium wires and rods (26.18% FY24, 13.17% FY25, 33.69% FY26 of total revenue from operations)
- Job work services revenue contribution (2.68% FY24, 1.90% FY25, 0.54% FY26)
- Declining share of revenue from repeat customers (89.47% FY24 to 84.87% FY25 to 45.09% FY26)
- Improving EBITDA margin (3.51% FY24 to 8.84% FY25 to 11.91% FY26) and PAT margin (0.73% FY24 to 4.16% FY25 to 6.77% FY26)
- Geographic revenue concentration in Uttar Pradesh (47.04% of FY26 revenue) and Delhi (19.56% of FY26 revenue)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Expansion of production capabilities in the High Tension (HT) and Medium Voltage Covered Conductor (MVCC) cable segments at the existing Plot No. 18/31, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad manufacturing facility

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company proposes to expand its existing manufacturing facility at Plot No. 18/31, Site-IV, Industrial Area, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, by installing a 6-33 kV Triple Layer Continuous Catenary Vulcanization (CCV) Line and a rigid stranding machine, along with construction of an additional shed and related civil/structural works, to build out HT and MVCC cable manufacturing capability. The CCV Line is expected to enhance installed capacity, improve insulation uniformity and process control, and reduce rejection/material wastage; the rigid stranding machine is expected to support in-house stranding of aluminium and copper wires into conductor cores. Certain state electricity utilities (including Maharashtra) prescribe CCV-based insulation curing technology for specified voltage-grade cables, and the expansion is intended to enable compliance and participation in tenders requiring CCV-based manufacturing. Upon completion, installed manufacturing capacity at this facility is expected to increase from approximately 1,500 km per annum to approximately 6,000 km per annum (per Project Report dated June 4, 2026 issued by Chartered Engineer Mr. Rajul Garg, Garg and Associates).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vendor registrations and approvals from multiple state-owned DISCOMs across India, obtained directly or under central/state schemes (RDSS, MUJY, MKVSY PH-II), supporting tender participation
- In-house manufacturing facilities (three plants in Ghaziabad, UP) supported by BIS product certifications and ISO management-system certifications
- Geographically dispersed customer base - sold products across 14 states and 1 Union Territory in Fiscal 2026
- Experienced Promoter, Vishal Jain, with over 22 years of experience in the wires, cables, conductors and winding wires industry

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Concentration of revenue in Government/DISCOM customers via tender-based procurement — A major portion of revenue is derived from state-owned DISCOMs; any reduction in Government expenditure, adverse changes in procurement policies, or failure to qualify for/secure tenders could adversely affect business, revenue and profitability.
- Absence of long-term supply contracts with Government customers — Engagements with DISCOMs are contingent on award of specific tenders (directly or via EPC contractors); contract award, execution timelines and payment receipt depend on Government approvals and budgetary processes, creating order-inflow uncertainty.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Install a 6-33 kV Triple Layer CCV Line and rigid stranding machine at the Plot No. 18/31, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad facility to raise installed manufacturing capacity from approximately 1,500 km per annum to approximately 6,000 km per annum.**
- **Deploy net IPO proceeds towards funding capital expenditure for expansion of the existing manufacturing facility at Plot No. 18/31, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad.**
- **Deploy net IPO proceeds towards funding of working capital requirements.**
- **Deploy a portion of net IPO proceeds towards general corporate purposes.**
- **Expand production capabilities in the HT and MVCC cable segments to serve transmission/distribution demand driven by rural and urban electrification initiatives (Saubhagya 2.0, RDSS) and to enable compliance with CCV-based insulation …**
- **Management flags continued dependence on Government/DISCOM tender-based procurement, absence of long-term supply contracts, and exposure to Government spending/procurement policy changes as a risk to order inflow, revenue and profitability.**
